messages:
dana_platform: Heads-up — thinking out loud about agent vs gateway for collectors. We keep hitting memory spikes when we run per-tenant exporter fanout in the agent. Proposal: keep agent lightweight (single pipeline per signal, basic sampling) and push heavy exporter/aggregation to gateway. Thoughts?

kim_dev: I ran a repro last week. With 8 exporters per tenant the agent's RSS jumps ~2.3x under bursty spans. :grimacing:

sam_infra: Gateway helps consolidate egress and gives us a single place to do retry/backoff and rate-limit. But it also introduces extra hop and latency for low-latency customers. Need concrete numbers.

ravi_sre: What about hybrid: agent does per-signal minimal preprocessing + prefix/KV cache for repeated trace heads, gateway handles exporter fanout, per-tenant retention and long-term buffering. That keeps agent memory low while preserving fidelity. :thinking_face:

kim_dev: Hybrid seems reasonable. We also need to consider rollout UX — ops teams shouldn't have to manage two full config sets. Can we have the same top-level config that switches mode? e.g. `mode: agent-only | hybrid | gateway-only`

dana_platform: Agreed. UX: one API surface, flag to opt into gateway-offload for selected tenants/signals. Default = hybrid for hipsights customers.

sam_infra: Cost note: gateway offload centralizes egress bytes which increases outbound bandwidth on gateway infra but reduces per-host GPU/memory. Need egress quota policies per-tenant.

ravi_sre: Also retention. If gateway owns longer retention/export buffering we can attach export TTL per-tenant and compute egress cost estimates. But where do we store transient buffers? Disk vs in-memory queue vs managed msg queue?

kim_dev: Disk-backed queue + backpressure seems safest. In-memory gives latency but OOM risk. Maybe use small in-memory ring + spill to local SSD under pressure.

dana_platform: Implementation sketch: agent config snippet that routes only sampled spans and forwarded envelopes for gateway:
```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [gateway]
  extensions: [health_check]
  telemetry:
    metrics: true
```
Gateway config handles exporter fanout, per-tenant quotas, and retention TTLs.

kim_dev: For the sampling strategy — can we support both tail and head sampling? Tail sampling at gateway makes more sense since gateway sees whole trace and can decide on SLO-based filters. Agent can do head-sample for immediate reduction at edge.

sam_infra: Exactly. Head-sample on agent to knock down high-volume noisy sources; gateway performs deterministic tail-sample for accuracy. We should surface a rollout plan: start with head-sample enabled for noisy SDKs, then enable gateway tail-sample for selected tenants.

ravi_sre: Regarding backpressure, exporter backoff must propagate to agents. If gateway disk is filling, send a throttle message via control-plane channel or respond with 429 from the gateway exporter endpoint and let agent backoff throttle. Need metrics to detect persistent 429s and auto-scale.

otel-bot: memory-alert: gateway-prod-2 disk > 78% used (past 5m), dropping export throughput by 18%

kim_dev: Good catch. That bot alert supports adding an automated spill-to-remote queue fallback (S3-like) for long tail retention. But that's expensive. We should expose opt-in cheaper retention tiers to customers.

dana_platform: UX requirements for Console: 1) toggle for offload mode per-tenant 2) visible estimated egress cost before enabling 3) retention slider with quick cost estimate 4) timeline of sampling changes and canary rollout controls.

sam_infra: One more: telemetry tracing for the telemetry pipeline itself. We need trace headers through agent->gateway->exporter so we can root-cause where spans are dropped or delayed. Also cost attribution per-token/span for billing.

ravi_sre: Ok action items: (1) kim prepare a small perf test that simulates 10k tenants with 3 exporters each and measure agent RSS with/without fanout; (2) sam draft gateway backpressure protocol (HTTP 429 semantics + control-plane notify); (3) dana mock console toggles + cost UI; (4) kim + ravi prototype disk spill + S3 fallback. Aim for spike week next sprint.

dana_platform: +1. I'll start a short runbook for hybrid failure modes (gateway-down, disk-full, control-plane partition) and include rollback steps.

kim_dev: quick question — should we gate hybrid on region? e.g., for APAC latency-sensitive tenants we keep agent-only unless they opt-in to gateway in-region.

sam_infra: Yes, region-aware routing is a must. Gateway in same region or local gateway cluster. Otherwise egress RTT kills latency SLO.

ravi_sre: Cool. If no objections I'll open a design doc and link here. We can iterate on sampling defaults and retention policies there. :+1:
